Write .zenodo.json from _supplement.yml

Source: R/write-zenodo.R
write_zenodo.Rd

write_zenodo() reads _supplement.yml in path and writes a .zenodo.json file into the same folder. When Zenodo's GitHub integration archives a release, it reads this file for the record's metadata. When a repository has both .zenodo.json and CITATION.cff, Zenodo uses .zenodo.json.

Usage

write_zenodo(path = ".", overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The folder that holds _supplement.yml.

overwrite

If TRUE, replace an existing file.

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

The file holds:

  • title: "Supplemental materials for: " and paper-title.

  • version: version, the version of the site, such as "1.0.0".

  • upload_type: "software".

  • description: "Supplemental materials for: " and citation.

  • creators: each author as "Family, Given", with the ORCID iD and the affiliation, in the order of _supplement.yml.

  • license: the SPDX identifier in license.content, in lowercase. The license field of .zenodo.json takes one license id, so the code license is not written.

Empty values are left out. In each value, every run of spaces and line breaks becomes one space, and spaces at the start and end are removed. Values are otherwise written as they are, so Markdown such as *Journal* keeps its asterisks. YAML reads some values without quotes as numbers or as true/false, for example No or 1.10. Such a value is an error, so put it in quotes in _supplement.yml, as the template does.

Errors

The errors that these functions raise themselves have the class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not a single non-missing, non-empty character string, or overwrite is not TRUE or FALSE.

  • supplement_error_no_metadata: path has no _supplement.yml.

  • supplement_error_parse: the yaml package cannot read _supplement.yml. Examples are a [ or a { that is not closed, a key line indented with a tab, and a key given twice in one map. The message names the file and gives the message of the yaml package.

  • supplement_error_no_map: the file has no supplement: map.

  • supplement_error_missing_field: paper-title is missing or empty. For write_zenodo(), also citation.

  • supplement_error_field_type: a value that the function reads is a list (a one-item list included), a number, or true/false where one text value belongs, or license (and, for write_citation(), zenodo) is not a map.

  • supplement_error_doi: for write_citation(), zenodo.concept-doi or zenodo.version-doi, with its prefix removed, is not 10., four to nine digits, /, and a suffix with no spaces.

  • supplement_error_license: license.content (and, for write_citation(), license.code) is not empty and does not have the shape of an SPDX license id: letters or digits, then groups of one . or - and more letters or digits, and at most one + at the end. For example, CC BY 4.0 has spaces and GPL--3.0 has two hyphens in a row, so both are errors, and CC-BY-4.0 is not. The check does not test that SPDX or Zenodo knows the id. The template's page footer applies the same check, so such a value also stops the site render.

  • supplement_error_version: version is not empty and is not three whole numbers joined by ., each 0 or without a leading zero, such as 1.0.0 or 0.10.2.

  • supplement_error_authors: authors is missing, empty, or not a list of authors.

  • supplement_error_author_name: an author has no family or no given name.

  • supplement_error_orcid: an ORCID iD does not have the form 0000-0000-0000-0000, with or without https://orcid.org/ or http://orcid.org/ in front, or its last character is not the iD's check digit. The last character can be X.

  • supplement_error_file_exists: the output file exists and overwrite is FALSE. A folder at the output path is this error even when overwrite is TRUE. So is a link, also a link to a missing file, because a write would follow it.

  • supplement_error_write: the output file was opened, but writing it gave an error or a warning (R warns when the disk is full), or the file then has another size than the text.

See also

write_citation() for CITATION.cff.

Examples

site <- file.path(tempdir(), "my-supplement")
dir.create(site)
file.copy(
  system.file("template", "_supplement.yml", package = "supplement"),
  site
)
#> [1] TRUE
write_zenodo(site)
readLines(file.path(site, ".zenodo.json"))
#>  [1] "{"                                                                                                                             
#>  [2] "  \"title\": \"Supplemental materials for: Title of the paper\","                                                              
#>  [3] "  \"upload_type\": \"software\","                                                                                              
#>  [4] "  \"description\": \"Supplemental materials for: Author, A. A., & Author, B. B. (Year). Title of the paper. *Journal Name*.\","
#>  [5] "  \"creators\": ["                                                                                                             
#>  [6] "    {"                                                                                                                         
#>  [7] "      \"name\": \"Author, A. A.\""                                                                                             
#>  [8] "    },"                                                                                                                        
#>  [9] "    {"                                                                                                                         
#> [10] "      \"name\": \"Author, B. B.\""                                                                                             
#> [11] "    }"                                                                                                                         
#> [12] "  ],"                                                                                                                          
#> [13] "  \"license\": \"cc-by-4.0\""                                                                                                  
#> [14] "}"                                                                                                                             
unlink(site, recursive = TRUE)
